entities.summary:
The Battle of the Frigidus, fought on 5 and 6 September 394, was a pivotal event in the decline of the Western Roman Empire. It took place in the Vipava Valley, a strategic location in modern-day Slovenia, and involved the forces of Emperor Theodosius I and the usurper Eugenius. The battle marked a turning point in the struggle for dominance in the Western Empire, with Theodosius ultimately emerging victorious.

The battle itself was a brutal and bloody affair, with heavy casualties on both sides. The fighting lasted for two days, with Theodosius's forces ultimately gaining the upper hand. The outcome was a decisive victory for Theodosius, who was able to secure his position as the undisputed ruler of the Western Empire.

The legacy of the Battle of the Frigidus can be seen in the subsequent fragmentation of the Western Empire. The battle marked the beginning of a period of decline and instability that would eventually lead to the rise of barbarian kingdoms in the region. It also had a lasting impact on the development of the Eastern Roman Empire, which would go on to play a major role in the preservation of classical culture.

As Theodosius I himself acknowledged, the battle was a 'tremendous miracle' that allowed him to triumph over his enemies. The victory was seen as a divine endorsement of his rule, and it cemented his position as one of the most powerful men in the Western Empire.
